name: A320
mesh_airframe: Airbus A320-200 CFM (FGMEMBERS A320family / IDG-A32X model)
part_offset_note: offsets transcribed from the model's own assembly XML (A320-200-CFM.xml and its nested wing/engine XMLs); the parts are modelled about local origins
hinge_note: hinge lines estimated from each surface's own leading-edge geometry plus the part offset (assets_pipeline/estimate_hinges.py); verified on screen by gate5_realmesh, not assumed

gear_geometry.source: this config lists NO landing-gear part: the A320family gear models live under Models/LandingGears/ and are not among the parts above, and the fuselage's Gear* objects (GearLDoor, GearNWell, ...) are doors and wells, not tyres. With no gear vertices the converter anchors z on the FDM VRP and says so in mesh_origin_basis; adding the gear parts (and their assembly-XML offsets) is what would make z measured. Measured 2026-09-25 from the pinned commit: the lowest drawn vertex is a nacelle at -3.27 m

dimensions_m.source: Airbus A320 Aircraft Characteristics Airport and Maintenance Planning (ACAP), section 2-1-1 (overall length 37.57 m, height 11.76 m); span from the flown FDM's own <wingspan>

category.source: EASA TCDS A.064 (A320 family), certification basis JAR/CS-25 -- unverified here: from memory of the TCDS; 14 CFR 25.337 states the same load factors

n_z_pos_g.source: 14 CFR 25.337(b): positive limit manoeuvring load factor n = 2.1 + 24000/(W+10000), not less than 2.5 and need not exceed 3.8; 2.5 at the A320's weights

n_z_neg_g.source: 14 CFR 25.337(c): negative limit manoeuvring load factor not less than -1.0 up to V_C

speed_limit_kt.source: unverified here: from memory of the A320 FCOM Limitations (V_MO 350 KIAS); compared here against JSBSim calibrated airspeed without a position-error correction

m_mo.source: unverified here: from memory of the A320 FCOM Limitations (M_MO 0.82)

alpha_stall_deg.reason: the JSBSim A320 model states no alpha limit (no <alphalimits> element; grep of A320.xml, 2026-09-28); the type's alpha-protection thresholds are flight-control laws, not modelled here

limits.note: Measured 2026-09-28: the JSBSim A320 trims and flies at 370 kt CAS at 1500 m (V_MO + 20), so a run beyond the speed limit is reachable on this model and is the null test in tests/test_limits.py.
